Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:04 -0500
Subject: URGENT: Streaming chat p99 spike during morning peak

Priyom / Redwood team,

We saw a significant p99 latency spike on the streaming chat endpoint this morning (08:15–09:05 ET) that impacted ~30% of user sessions for our Live Triage workflow. Metrics attached — you can see p95 climbed from ~340ms to 1.8s and p99 to 4.6s; error rates also rose from 0.2% to 2.1% during the peak. Our support queue doubled and the on-call triage team is escalating.

This is a production-impacting incident for Revere Health — we need immediate mitigation and a concrete timeline for resolution. Please let us know:
- What short-term steps you will take to stop the customer impact?
- What root cause you are investigating?
- Whether this will trigger any SLA credits (we're currently on the Growth plan).

Attaching a short telemetry dump (revere_peak_telemetry_0214.pdf) and a sample SSE trace (sse_p99_trace_0214.csv). I will be available by phone.

— Liam
Director, Platform Operations
Revere Health

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Triage Oncall <oncall@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:45:12 -05:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Streaming chat p99 spike during morning peak — initial technical findings

Quick update from triage (prelim):
- Confirmed: impact is concentrated on the SSE streaming path for tenant revere_health; WebSocket traffic shows elevated but smaller tail.
- Correlated event: a burst of concurrent long-lived sessions between 08:10–08:50 ET caused cache pressure on prefix/KV lookup and increased batching latency in the realtime pump.
- Observable: a regression in the nonlinear scheduling path where batching threshold logic (v2.3.1) allowed large micro-batches to form under this traffic distribution, which pushed token emission into high tail latency.

Attachments: I exported a per-request trace for the affected period (sse_p99_trace_0214.csv) and a short heap/worker snapshot. The CSV contains request IDs and stage timing (accept->batch->emit).

Immediate mitigations applied (09:30 ET):
1) Adjusted batching threshold down to force smaller batches (hotfix config patch) — expected immediate p99 reduction.
2) Rerouted Revere traffic to the lower-latency dedicated pool in us-east-1 (temporary).
3) Enabled stricter KV cache TTL for prefix lookups to reduce cache misses.

Estimated timeline: we expect visible p99 improvement within 10–20 minutes after the routing change and full stabilization in ~60–90 minutes. Root cause analysis continues; initial hypothesis: a combination of skewed session duration and the newer batching optimizer (v2.3.1) that behaves poorly on extreme session-length distributions.

Next steps:
- Roll back batching optimizer to the prior safe threshold for the affected zone if we see continued tail after 90 minutes.
- Produce a short postmortem with regression windows, metrics, and recommended runtime fix (INF-4829).

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
